parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the balancing of a metre rule. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 3.1. Fig. 3.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Place the metre rule on the pivot, with its scale facing upwards, so that the metre rule is as near as possible to being balanced. Record the scale reading S on the metre rule at the point where the rule balances on the pivot. S = ................................................... cm [1]

ms.label: 3(a)
ms.text: S in range 50.0 ± 2.0 (cm) recorded to the nearest mm

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) • Place object Q with its centre on the metre rule at the 90.0 cm mark. • Place a load P of weight P = 1.0 N on the metre rule.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Adjust the position of the load P so that the metre rule is as near as possible to being balanced. The pivot must remain directly below the scale reading S . Measure, and record in Table 3.1, the distance a from the centre of load P to the centre of load Q, as shown in Fig. 3.2. [1] Fig. 3.2

ms.label: 3(b)(i)
ms.text: first a value recorded in cm

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Repeat the steps above, using loads of weight P = 2.0 N, 3.0 N, 4.0 N and 5.0 N. Record all the values of a in Table 3.1. Table 3.1 P / N a / cm 1 P / 1 N 1.0 1.00 2.0 0.50 3.0 0.33 4.0 0.25 5.0 0.20 [3]

ms.label: 3(b)(ii)
ms.text:
a values decreasing
a values all to the nearest mm
a values all > 45.0 cm

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Plot a graph of a / cm ( y -axis) against 1 P / 1 N ( x -axis). Start the y -axis at a / cm = 30. Start the x -axis at 0. [4]

ms.label: 3(c)
ms.text:
axes correctly labelled with quantity and unit and correct way round
suitable scales with a axis starting from 30
all plots correct to ½ small square
good line judgement, thin, continuous line

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Record the value of a when 1 P = 0. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. a = ......................................................... [2]

ms.label: 3(d)
ms.text:
method clearly shown on graph
value correct to ± ½ small square
